newsitem.title: USA: Emergency crews clean up after Calif. derailment.
newsitem.headline: Emergency crews clean up after Calif. derailment.

text.p: Emergency crews Saturday worked to stabilize freight cars that derailed and tumbled down a canyon slope near Martinez, Calif., forcing the evacuation of residents in the area, authorities said.

"Right now we're stabilizing them (the cars) in place to make sure they're not leaking and then we'll pull them out one at a time," Contra Costa County Sheriff Lt. Scott Daly said. "We hope to have people back in their homes this evening."

The accident occurred late on Friday about 25 miles (40 km) northeast of San Francisco. The two-locomotive, 60-car Burlington Northern Santa Fe train was traveling to nearby Richmond, Calif., when it jumped the tracks.

At least 19 cars of the train carrying gas residue and corrosive acid derailed in the accident, prompting the evacuation of homes within a half mile of the site as a precaution. There have been no reports of injuries or leaks, and the cause of the derailment is under investigation.
PG&E Corp's Pacific Gas and Electric Co. cut off gas and electric service to homes in the immediate area to eliminate any possible "source of ignition," PG&E spokesman Lyle LaFaver said.

Daly said once the freight cars were stabilized, they would be pulled from the canyon area and moved out on trucks. "There is a risk when they start moving these things of fire and a slight risk of explosion," Daly said.

Of the 19 cars that derailed, 10 contained liquefied petroleum gas residue, two were carrying phosphoric acid and one was full of paint, Burlington Northern spokesman Michael Martin said. The other cars that derailed were carrying wheat, tin products and fiber board. Both cars containing acid were upright and did not tumble down the canyon.

Martin said the accident damaged a large section of track, forcing Burlington Northern to detour some of its trains. But he said repair crews were expected to reopen the line -- which carries 20 or more freight trains each day to and from the San Francisco Bay area -- later Saturday.
